newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian coalition, Congress play down Rao's woes.
newsitem.headline: Indian coalition, Congress play down Rao's woes.

text.p: India's centre-left coalition and its make-or-break ally Congress shrugged off legal troubles plaguing former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and said his woes posed no threat to the new government.
Rao was charged on Thursday in a forgery case and was denied legal protection against arrest in a separate conspiracy case.
Rao's difficulties emboldened the Hindu nationalist opposition, which predicted growing strains between the 13-party United Front coalition and Congress.
"Our confidence has gone up," said L.K. Advani, president of the rightist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The United Front and Congress joined hands to topple a 12-day-old BJP government following general elections ending last May that returned the BJP as the largest single group in parliament.

Senior BJP leader Jaswant Singh, who was finance minister in the short-lived BJP government, said the charges against Rao spelled trouble for the United Front, especially in important local polls in populous Uttar Pradesh starting next week.
But United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy denied any threat to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority government.
"There is no reason why these cases should have any impact on the longevity or durability or stability of the Deve Gowda government," Reddy told a news conference.
"There is absolutely no room to think that the Congress party will review its position on the issue at all."
Deve Gowda's coalition lacks an outright majority in the 545-seat lower house of parliament and depends on the support of Congress's 140 deputies.
Congress finished second in the recent general elections behind the BJP, which stepped down when it failed to muster enough support to win a confidence vote.
Indian stock markets fell on Friday on worries that Rao's legal problems could stir political uncertainty. The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index shed 1.58 percent to close at 3,254.73 points.
Congress general secretary Devendra Dwivedi was asked if the two cases in which Rao had been named had implications for the party's support for Deve Gowda's United Front government.
"I don't think there is any threat to the United Front government arising out of what has happened, immediately," Dwivedi told Reuters.

Rao stepped down as Congress chief last Saturday after a court upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court on September 30 in the criminal conspiracy case. Dwivedi said Rao would remain head of the Congress parliamentary party, which includes all deputies in the federal parliament.
Rao's lawyer said on Thursday that he expected his client to be arrested on Monday, when Rao is due to appear in a Delhi court in the conspiracy case.
A court on Thursday rejected Rao's plea for anticipatory bail, which would have protected him against arrest. Legal experts said he could request ordinary bail if arrested.

Newspapers said authorities were preparing for the possibility that the former prime minister might be arrested in the cheating case and put under police custody ahead of the trial. Rao has denied any involvement in the 13-year-old case.

The Asian Age newspaper said authorities were preparing a bungalow in central Delhi as a "special prison" for Rao. One official said there was a possibility that Rao, if arrested, would be confined to his home.
